name: Independent on Sunday cryptic crossword No 1,355

clue.text: Hot drink is brought to European carriage

blocks.note: cha (or char) is British slang for tea
taken as written
E is the standard abbreviation for European

explanation.surface: A cup of tea is served to someone sitting in a European railway carriage.
explanation.definitionFit: A chaise is a light horse-drawn vehicle, an example of a carriage for one or two travellers.

clue.text: School group of excellent quality

blocks.note: first meaning: a set of pupils taught together
second meaning: informal adjective

explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as praise for a school group; it is two separate meanings of one word, noun and informal adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun names pupils taught together, while the informal adjective praises something stylish or top-rate, as in a class act.

clue.text: Digression about Irish in part of Heathrow?

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece wraps round the other here

blocks.note: an aside is a remark straying from the main subject
IR is the abbreviation for Irish

explanation.surface: A rambling speech about the Irish delivered somewhere in London's Heathrow airport.
explanation.walkthrough: Heathrow is London's main airport; the question mark flags that the definition is by example, since every airport has this zone.
explanation.definitionFit: Airside is the zone of an airport beyond passport and security control, so it is one region of Heathrow.

clue.text: Set point in play! Hurry up!

indicators.note: in play suggests letters being moved about loosely, as a ball is in a game

blocks.note: a tennis term, used here only for its letters

explanation.surface: A tennis umpire urging players to get on with the game at set point.
explanation.walkthrough: The tennis setting makes 'in play' sound like live action on court; it is the signal to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a colloquial urging to go faster, originally to a driver pressing the accelerator, matching a shouted demand for speed.

clue.text: Republicans beat Democrats ultimately and succeed

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so only the final letter of that word is kept

blocks.note: the Grand Old Party, the US Republican Party
to lace is to thrash or beat
the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: An American election report: the Republicans defeated the Democrats in the end and won.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beat' looks like the verb of the election story but supplies a synonym meaning thrash.
explanation.definitionFit: To go places is an idiom for being successful and making progress in life or a career.

clue.text: Verse, art, one translated - excessively serious

indicators.note: translated means turned into another form, so the letters are converted into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Poetry and art rendered into another language come out far too solemn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Translated' fits the poetry picture but signals rearranging the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Over- adds the sense of too much to earnest, which means grave and sincere, giving overly solemn.

clue.text: Gloomy lair at bottom of field

blocks.note: a lea is a meadow, a poetic word for a field
a den is an animal's lair

explanation.surface: A dark animal's lair hidden at the foot of a meadow.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'at bottom of' puts the lair below the field, so the field comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: Leaden describes a dull, heavy, grey sky or mood, figuratively dark and depressing like lead.

clue.text: Prisoner beginning, we hear, to accept defeat

indicators.note: we hear says a word is to be taken by its sound, not its spelling

blocks.note: con is short for convict
a seed is the beginning of something; the word sounds like a verb meaning yield

explanation.surface: A convict starting his sentence decides to give in.
explanation.definitionFit: To concede is to admit that one has lost, as a candidate does after an election count.

clue.text: Irregular payment of small figure in London area? Right

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other, which acts as its surround

blocks.note: SE is the south-east London postal district, an example hence the question mark
wee is Scottish for small
a number, any figure will do
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A dodgy cash payment for a small statue in some London district, okay?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Small figure' reads as a statuette but splits into two pieces, an adjective and a number.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweetener is a bribe or inducement, a payment made outside proper channels to win favour.

clue.text: Regularly visited Algarve with journalist? Yes

indicators.note: visiting regularly means calling at every other point, so alternate letters are taken

blocks.note: the odd-numbered letters
ED is short for editor, the usual crossword journalist

explanation.surface: Asked whether they often went to the Algarve with a reporter, someone answers yes.
explanation.walkthrough: The Algarve is Portugal's southern coast; 'visited' belongs to the selection signal, not the story.
explanation.definitionFit: Agreed! is said as an exclamation of assent, so it can stand for yes in reply.

clue.text: In canteen I ate daily on return, being confined

indicators.note: In says the letters sit inside the following words of the clue
on return means coming back, so the letters are read from right to left

blocks.note: the letters straddling the words

explanation.surface: Someone who eats in a canteen every day when back, like a prisoner fed in a mess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Being' is a noun here, a person, so the definition is a confined person.
explanation.definitionFit: A detainee is a person held in custody, a creature kept locked up rather than free.

clue.text: One with hump as these hopes drift sadly?

indicators.note: sadly suggests things going wrong, so the letters fall into disorder

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone in a sulk, 'got the hump', as their hopes fade away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Having the hump' is British slang for being sulky, which the surface plays on; here the hump is literal.
explanation.definitionFit: Ship of the desert is the traditional nickname for the camel, the animal famous for its hump.

clue.text: How rent is paid adhering to every detail

blocks.note: first meaning, read cryptically: a tenant pays money over to the landlord, the one who lets
second meaning: the idiom for following instructions exactly

explanation.walkthrough: A letter here is not a written message but someone who lets property, so rent goes to that person.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means precisely and literally, obeying instructions in every particular.

clue.text: No contemporary writing about this period

definitions.text: No contemporary writing about this period

blocks.clueFragment: No contemporary writing about this period
blocks.note: surface reading: an age that no modern author has written about
setter's reading: an era from which no written records survive, because writing had not been invented

explanation.walkthrough: 'Contemporary' seems to mean modern; it means from the same time, so nobody living then wrote anything down.
explanation.definitionFit: The term names the span of human existence before written records began, known only from archaeology.

clue.text: Liking country film about a threesome, titillating initially

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word just before it
about means surrounding, so one piece goes round the rest

blocks.note: pic is short for picture, a film
taken as written
a trio is a group of three
the opening letter

explanation.surface: A racy film about a ménage à trois, the sort a country-loving person might enjoy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Country' suggests rural life, but it means one's nation.
explanation.definitionFit: Patriotic describes devotion to and love of one's nation, so it means fond of one's homeland.

clue.text: Refusal in Paris to make case for English element

indicators.note: a case holds something, so one piece becomes the casing round another

blocks.note: non is French for no
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: A French refusal to argue in favour of some English element.
explanation.definitionFit: Neon is a chemical element, a noble gas used in glowing advertising signs.

clue.text: “Yes” in German firm to snack for rebel

blocks.note: ja is German for yes
Co is short for company
a bite is a quick snack

explanation.surface: A German company agreeing to provide snacks for an insurgent.
explanation.walkthrough: Jacobites were supporters of the exiled Stuart kings who rose against the British crown in 1715 and 1745.
explanation.definitionFit: A Jacobite rebelled in support of James II and his descendants, so the word names a historical insurgent.

clue.text: Novice lodged in city rooms

indicators.note: lodged in says the letters are staying inside the words that follow

blocks.note: the letters bridging the two words

explanation.surface: A beginner lives in rented rooms in town.
explanation.definitionFit: A tyro is a beginner or learner, someone new to a skill or trade.

clue.text: Nautical equipment sailor brought up on course

indicators.note: in a down entry, brought up means read from bottom to top

blocks.note: tar is an old word for a seaman
a line is a course or route

explanation.surface: Ship's gear that a sailor raised while sailing a set route.
explanation.definitionFit: Ratlines are small ropes fixed across a ship's shrouds to form ladder rungs for climbing the rigging.

clue.text: Old vehicle - van caterer refurbished

indicators.note: refurbished means done up and reworked, so the letters are rebuilt in another order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An old catering van has been restored.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a veteran car is specifically one built before 1905, older than a vintage car.
explanation.definitionFit: A veteran car is a very early motor car, so an old vehicle by definition.

clue.text: Ivy perhaps, chilly at first, then flexible

indicators.note: at first means only the opening letter of the word before it counts

blocks.note: the opening letter
limber means supple

explanation.surface: Ivy, stiff in the cold at first, later becomes pliable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps' marks ivy as one example of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Ivy is a plant that grows upward by clinging to walls and trees, so it is an example of a climbing plant.

clue.text: Clever Bishop supported by Conservative

blocks.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
the right is the conservative wing of politics

explanation.surface: A shrewd bishop is backed by a Tory politician.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'supported by' puts the second piece underneath the first.
explanation.definitionFit: Bright describes someone intelligent and quick-witted, a common synonym for smart.

clue.text: Abroad, note invite isn't primarily required by him?

definitions.text: Abroad, note invite isn't primarily required by him?

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so only the opening letter of the next word is used
abroad suggests being scattered widely, so the letters are spread into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written, apostrophe dropped
the opening letter

explanation.surface: A meddler in foreign affairs notes that he needs no invitation to act abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: someone who gets involved overseas without being asked.
explanation.definitionFit: An interventionist favours involvement in other countries' affairs, uninvited if need be.

clue.text: Recurring idea in article on Maine

blocks.note: the definite article
ME is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Maine

explanation.surface: A newspaper feature about the state of Maine keeps returning to the same idea.
explanation.definitionFit: A theme is a subject or motif that comes back repeatedly through a work of art or argument.

clue.text: Soldiers smuggling gun into French island drive dangerously

indicators.note: something smuggled is carried hidden inside, so one piece goes within another

blocks.note: the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve force
ile is French for island
gat is old slang for a pistol

explanation.surface: Troops sneaking a weapon onto an island off France.
explanation.walkthrough: Strictly it is the island that takes in the gun; the soldiers simply stand in front.
explanation.definitionFit: To tailgate is to follow another vehicle too closely, a risky habit on the road.

clue.text: 51 up to it and legally answerable

blocks.note: LI is 51 in Roman numerals
capable

explanation.surface: Someone aged fifty-one is still fit for the job and responsible under the law.
explanation.walkthrough: A bare number in a clue often wants its Roman numeral.
explanation.definitionFit: Liable means responsible in law, bound to pay damages or bear the consequences.

clue.text: Living being, rare, cute, evolving

indicators.note: evolving means changing form over time, so the letters develop into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A description of some rare, adorable animal in the course of evolution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Evolving' fits the natural-history picture perfectly but signals rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: A creature is any animal or person, something alive and existing.

clue.text: Award daughter, for one, always rejected

indicators.note: rejected suggests being thrown back, so the word is read backwards

blocks.note: D is the abbreviation for daughter
e.g., for example
e'er is the poetic contraction of ever

explanation.surface: A daughter, for example, whose prize is forever refused.
explanation.definitionFit: A degree is the qualification a university confers on a graduate, an academic honour.
